name: Financial
tagline: What the township raises, what it spends, what it owes, and what it has set aside.
primer: A lower-tier Ontario municipality raises most of its own-source revenue through the property tax levy. Council does not set a tax bill directly. It sets a levy — the total dollars the township needs from taxation — and that levy is divided across the assessment base by property class using rates and ratios. If assessment grows, the same levy produces a lower rate. If assessment is frozen, as Ontario's has been through several postponed reassessment cycles, the rate must rise for the levy to rise. This is why 'the rate went up' and 'taxes went up' are different statements, and why both can be true or false independently.

The bill a North Glengarry ratepayer receives carries three portions: the township levy, the United Counties of SDG levy, and the education levy set by the province. Township council controls the first. It votes on the second as part of county council but not alone. It controls none of the third. Any statement about 'the tax increase' has to say which portion it means.

Municipal budgets are split into operating and capital, and the two behave differently. Operating covers the cost of running the place this year — wages, fuel, insurance, contracts, winter control — and must be balanced by law; an Ontario municipality cannot budget for a deficit. Capital covers building and replacing assets whose life extends over many years, and is funded from a mix of reserves, debt, grants, and a transfer from the operating budget. That transfer, the contribution to capital and reserves, is the number that reveals whether a municipality is funding renewal or deferring it.

Reserves and reserve funds are the municipality's savings, and the distinction matters. Reserves are discretionary: council can redirect them. Reserve funds are set aside for a defined purpose, and obligatory reserve funds — development charges, gas tax, parkland — are restricted by statute and cannot be spent on anything else. A reserve balance that looks healthy in total may be mostly restricted money. Always read reserves by purpose, never as a single figure.

Debt is constrained rather than prohibited. The province caps annual debt repayment at 25 percent of own-source revenue through the Annual Repayment Limit, calculated by the ministry from the Financial Information Return. Being far below the limit is not automatically prudence and being near it is not automatically distress: it depends on what the debt bought and whether the asset it funded is still delivering service.

The Financial Information Return is the backbone of this domain. Every Ontario municipality files one annually on the same schedules, which makes it the only genuinely multi-year, comparable financial source available without transcribing budget books. It is filed months after year end, so the most recent year here will usually lag. Audited statements carry the detail the return flattens, and budget by-laws carry the plan the actuals are measured against.

tierSplit.note: Set by township council in the annual budget and rate by-law.
Set by SDG county council, apportioned across member municipalities by weighted assessment. Township council members sit on county council.
Rates set by the province. Neither council has any discretion over this portion.
Valued by MPAC, a provincial corporation. The municipality does not assess property and cannot change a valuation.

gaps: Budget-versus-actual by department requires pairing each year's budget by-law with the same year's audited statements. Departmental groupings change between documents and must be reconciled by hand.

Grants received by program are not reported as a single series anywhere. They have to be assembled from council reports, the Financial Information Return revenue schedules, and individual grant agreements.
The comparator municipality set has not been chosen. No comparison is shown until the sponsor confirms which municipalities are fair.

indicators.name: Township tax levy, total
indicators.tierNote: Township portion only. Excludes the county levy and the education levy, which appear on the same tax bill but are set elsewhere.
indicators.definition: Total dollars raised from property taxation for township purposes in the year, as levied by the annual tax rate by-law. Excludes payments in lieu of taxes, user fees, and grants.

indicators.name: Township levy per household
indicators.definition: Total township levy divided by the number of occupied private dwellings. A distribution average, not an average tax bill: it does not account for property class mix, and no individual household pays this figure.
indicators.methodology: Levy from the Financial Information Return; household count interpolated between census years and held flat between them. The interpolation is why intercensal years are marked as estimated.

indicators.name: Operating expenses, actual
indicators.definition: Total operating expenditure for the year on a Financial Information Return basis, before amortization adjustments. Excludes capital expenditure.

indicators.name: Capital expenditure, actual
indicators.definition: Actual capital expenditure in the year across all asset categories, on a Financial Information Return basis. Capital spending is lumpy by nature: a single bridge or plant upgrade can double a year's figure, so read the five-year pattern rather than any one year.

indicators.name: Reserves and reserve funds, year-end balance
indicators.definition: Combined year-end balance of discretionary reserves and reserve funds, including obligatory reserve funds. The total is not freely spendable: obligatory reserve funds such as development charges and the Canada Community-Building Fund are restricted by statute. Read the balance by purpose in the detail table below before drawing any conclusion from the total.

indicators.name: Reserves per household
indicators.definition: Total reserves and reserve funds divided by occupied private dwellings. Used because absolute reserve balances are not readable across time as population changes. Household counts between census years are interpolated.

indicators.name: Long-term debt outstanding
indicators.definition: Principal outstanding on long-term debt at year end, for township purposes. Excludes debt issued by the county or other bodies.

series.note: Step-up reflects new issuance; confirm which project against the debenture by-law.

indicators.name: Debt servicing as a share of own-source revenue
indicators.definition: Annual principal and interest payments on long-term debt expressed as a percentage of own-source revenue. The province caps this at 25 percent through the Annual Repayment Limit. Distance from the limit describes borrowing room, not whether past borrowing was sound.
indicators.methodology: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing calculates the Annual Repayment Limit from the Financial Information Return and issues it to the municipality. Use the ministry figure rather than recomputing it.

indicators.name: Operating contribution to capital and reserves
indicators.definition: Dollars transferred from the operating budget to capital and to reserves in the year. This is the amount of current-year taxation being applied to renewing assets rather than to running services, and it is the operating-side counterpart to the renewal funding gap in the infrastructure domain.

indicators.name: Grants and transfers received
indicators.tierNote: Provincial and federal transfers received by the township. Excludes transfers to the county.
indicators.definition: Total conditional and unconditional grants received from the provincial and federal governments in the year, operating and capital combined. Capital grants are episodic and drive most of the year-to-year movement.

series.note: Elevated year; confirm whether pandemic-era transfers are included.

indicators.name: Total assessment base
indicators.tierNote: Assessed by MPAC, a provincial corporation. The township cannot alter valuations.
indicators.definition: Total current value assessment across all property classes for taxation purposes. Movement in this figure reflects new construction and appeals, not market appreciation, because the province has held the valuation date fixed through several postponed reassessment cycles.

tables.title: Reserves and reserve funds by purpose, year end
tables.description: Discretionary reserves can be redirected by council. Obligatory reserve funds are restricted by statute and cannot be applied to another purpose. The restricted share is what separates a usable balance from a headline one.

source.locator: Note on reserves and reserve funds

tables.note: The development charges row shows zero because it is not yet confirmed whether the township has a development charges by-law in force. Confirm before reading the zero as a balance rather than an absence of the instrument.

tables.title: Township tax rates by property class
tables.description: Township portion only. The county and education portions are additional and are set by other bodies. Rates are expressed as a percentage of current value assessment.
tables.note: Tax ratios govern how the levy is distributed between classes. Changing a ratio shifts burden between classes without changing the total levy — a distinct decision from changing the levy itself.

tables.title: Budget versus actual by department, most recent closed year
tables.description: Variance is stated as actual minus budget. A positive figure is spending above the approved budget; a negative figure is spending below it. Neither is described here as favourable or unfavourable — the reason for a variance is what matters, and it is found in the year-end report to council.
tables.note: Departmental groupings differ between the budget by-law and the audited statements. Reconciliation is manual and should be re-checked whenever either document changes format.

tables.title: Major capital projects: budget, spend to date, status
tables.description: Projects with an approved budget above $250,000. Spend to date is as at the most recent report to council, which is not always year end — the reporting date is given per project.

rows.project: County road reconstruction through settlement area

tables.note: The final row is a county project inside township boundaries. It is shown because residents experience it as local work, and excluded from township capital totals because the township neither budgets nor controls it.
